What BOOM is

Not an agency. Your agent.

In the Netherlands this role has a name: aanhuurmakelaar, an agent hired by the tenant and paid only by the tenant. We don't list apartments, we don't represent landlords, and we don't take a cent from the other side of the table. We find, we apply, we negotiate, and we read the contract before you sign it.

We work exclusively for you. BOOM Amsterdam never accepts fees, commissions or referrals from landlords, their agents, or listing platforms. Dutch law forbids an agent from charging both sides of a rental, and we agree with it: an agent paid by the landlord cannot negotiate your rent down.

You pay for the work, not the outcome of a game we rigged. Our fee covers search, dossier, applications, viewings and contract review. Your €99 founding deposit is refundable before work starts and is deducted from your service fee.

Before you sign

Six things most internationals discover after signing.

The deposit cap

Dutch law caps the deposit at two months' rent. Agents still ask for three. We don't let them.

Registration

A landlord cannot forbid you from registering at the address (BRP). No registration means no BSN, no bank, no healthcare. We confirm it in writing before you pay.

The points system

Many Amsterdam apartments fall under rent regulation by the points system (WWS). If the asking rent is above the legal maximum, you have leverage. We run the check.

Service costs

"Rent €1,800 + €250 service costs" often hides unlawful charges. We separate what's legitimate from what's padding.

Contract type

Since 2024 the default rental contract in the Netherlands is indefinite. Fixed-term offers are the exception and have conditions. We check which one you're being handed.

Income rules

Starting a new job, freelancing, or paid in a non-euro currency? There's a right way to present each of these. We write it so it reads as safe to a Dutch landlord.

Questions

Straight answers.

Isn't it illegal for agents to charge tenants in the Netherlands?

It's illegal for an agent to charge you when they also act for the landlord, which is what most "free" agencies do. An agent you hire, who works only for you, may charge you for the work. That is exactly what we are, and it's the only reason we can negotiate on your side.

How fast will I have an apartment?

With a complete dossier and applications inside the hour, most of our searches should close in two to six weeks depending on budget and move-in date. Nobody can promise a date in Amsterdam. Anyone who does is selling you something else.

What is the €99 deposit?

It reserves one of the ten founding spots and locks the founding price for life. It's refundable any time before we start working, and it's deducted from your fee once we do.

What if you don't find anything?

Then we talk. The fee pays for a defined amount of work, and we'll be honest in the first call if your budget and timeline don't fit the market. We'd rather refund your deposit than take a search we don't believe in.

Why only ten clients?

Because we can serve ten properly. BOOM Amsterdam is one local person and one portal, not a call centre. The cap is what makes the speed real.

I'm moving from Rome with BOOM. Does this work for me?

Especially for you. Your dossier is already in the portal. Message us and we'll convert it to the Dutch format the same day.
